policies.reject.policy.document_malforme: The bundle is not valid YAML. The parser said: {detail}
policies.reject.policy.schema_version_un: schema_version {found} is not supported. This server understands {supported}.
policies.reject.policy.tenant_missing: The bundle names no tenant. Add a tenant line: the tenant selects which compiled program is served.
policies.reject.policy.no_rules: The bundle has no rules. Add at least one: an empty bundle denies everything by default and says nothing about why.
policies.reject.policy.timezone_unknown: Time zone {timezone} is not a known IANA location. Use a name such as Europe/Lisbon, or leave the key out for UTC.
policies.reject.policy.label_vocabulary_: Label key {label_key} declares no values. List the values a rule may match, or remove the key.
policies.reject.policy.group_vocabulary_: The group list contains an empty name. Remove it.
policies.reject.rule.id_missing: This rule has no id. Give it one: the id is what an explanation names and what an operator searches for.
policies.reject.rule.id_duplicate: Rule id {id} is already used at line {other_line}. An id identifies its rule in every explanation and audit record, so each must be unique.
policies.reject.rule.unreachable: This rule can never match: rule {shadowed_by} at line {other_line} already matches everything it does. Narrow this rule, or move it above {shadowed_by}.
policies.reject.rule.effect_missing: This rule states no effect. Add effect: allow or effect: deny.
policies.reject.rule.deny_carries_route: A deny rule carries a route. A denied connection has no snapshot, so remove the route block or make the rule an allow.
policies.reject.rule.allow_needs_route: An allow rule carries no route. Add a route block: an allow with no snapshot is a connection with no policy.
policies.reject.rule.deny_needs_reason: A deny rule carries no reason. Add one: it is what an operator reads when they resolve the decision id.
policies.reject.match.unknown_group: Group {group} is not declared in the bundle's groups list. Declare it there, or correct the spelling.
policies.reject.match.unknown_label_key: Label key {label_key} is not declared in the bundle's labels map. Declare it there, or correct the spelling.
policies.reject.match.unknown_label_valu: Label {label_key}={label_value} is not declared in the bundle's labels map. Declare the value there, or correct the spelling.
policies.reject.match.invalid_cidr: {cidr} is not a valid address or CIDR prefix.
policies.reject.match.invalid_hostname_p: {pattern} is not a valid hostname pattern. Use an exact name, or one leading wildcard such as *.prod.example.com.
policies.reject.match.empty_term: The {axis} match declares {term} with no values. List at least one, or remove the key: an empty list matches nothing, and is almost never what was meant.
policies.reject.route.intent_missing: The route states no intent. Add intent: direct or intent: hops-permitted.
policies.reject.route.channels_missing: The route has no channels key. State the channel types: an empty list denies every one and is a policy, but leaving the key out is not.
policies.reject.route.filter_mode_missin: The route's filter policy states no mode. Add mode: whitelist or mode: blacklist: a filter with no defined default can fail open by omission.
policies.reject.route.forward_destinatio: The route permits the {channel} channel but names no forwarding destinations. Add forwards.{list}: an unconstrained forwarding axis is a mistake, not a wildcard.
policies.reject.route.subsystems_missing: The route permits subsystems but names none. List them: sftp can be denied on its own only if subsystems are named one by one.
policies.reject.route.filter_policy_both: The route's filter policy sets both a rule list and a restricted-exec allow-list. The two tiers are alternatives, never layers: keep one.
policies.reject.route.restricted_exec_em: The route sets exec_mode: restricted but names no commands, so it denies every exec. If that is the intent, say so with an empty channels or requests list instead.
policies.reject.route.invalid_destinatio: {destination} is not a valid forwarding destination. Use a host, a wildcard such as *.prod, or a CIDR prefix, with an optional port or port range.
policies.reject.route.ladder_empty: The route declares a credentials ladder with no entries. List at least one method, or remove the key to leave the proxy its own configured method.
policies.reject.route.exec_mode_mismatch: The route declares a restricted-exec allow-list, but its exec_mode is not restricted, so the list would never decide anything. Set exec_mode: restricted, or remove the list.
policies.reject.route.session_deadline_i: Session deadline {duration} is not a positive duration. Use a form such as 8h or 45m.
policies.reject.route.concurrency_invali: Concurrency cap {field} is negative. Use a positive cap, or 0 for none.
policies.reject.route.algorithm_floor_pr: The route sets algorithm floor {floor} with algorithm profile {profile}, which widens the key-exchange axis the floor narrows. A proxy refuses the pair because the leg could never connect: drop the floor, or use the default or legacy-rsa-sha1 profile.
policies.reject.route.algorithm_ban_empt: Entry {index} of algorithm_bans.{axis} is empty. Name the algorithm exactly as SSH spells it.
policies.reject.route.algorithm_ban_repe: algorithm_bans.{axis} lists {name} twice. List each identifier once: the record shows a ban exactly as it was issued.
policies.reject.cache.key_empty: The rule's cache hint names no key components, and a hint with no key is not cacheable. List what the key is derived from, or remove the hint.
policies.reject.cache.key_not_identity_b: The rule's cache key does not include subject. A key shared across identities would serve one user another user's policy.
policies.reject.cache.ttl_invalid: Cache lifetime {ttl} is not positive. A hint with no lifetime is not a hint: remove it, or give it one.
policies.reject.cache.hint_on_deny: A deny rule carries a cache hint. A proxy never reuses a denial, so the hint would never be read: remove it.
policies.reject.cache.key_component_dupl: Cache key component {component} is listed twice. Remove the duplicate.
policies.reject.credential.method_missin: Ladder entry {index} names no method. Every entry names one of the four the contract defines.
policies.reject.credential.username_miss: Ladder entry {index} ({method}) names no username. Every method requires one, and the proxy refuses the route at its first authorize call. Name the account, and never derive it from the identity's login.
policies.reject.credential.username_empt: Ladder entry {index} declares a literal username with no value. Write the account name.
policies.reject.credential.param_wrong_m: Ladder entry {index} sets {param}, which method {method} does not take. Remove it, or change the method.
policies.reject.credential.platform_miss: Ladder entry {index} is ephemeral-account and names no platform. It is never inferred: a wrong guess runs configuration commands against the wrong parser.
policies.reject.credential.credential_ki: Ladder entry {index} is ephemeral-account and names no credential_kind. Choose password or publickey: a default would hand out the weaker of two different exposures.
policies.reject.credential.expiry_postur: Ladder entry {index} is ephemeral-account and names no expiry_posture. Choose target-enforced, proxy-enforced or accepted-risk.
policies.reject.credential.lifetime_miss: Ladder entry {index} has expiry posture {posture} and no lifetime_seconds. A posture that enforces an expiry needs an expiry to enforce.
policies.reject.credential.lifetime_inva: Ladder entry {index} has lifetime_seconds {lifetime}. It must be positive.
policies.reject.credential.device_field_: Ladder entry {index} declares device field {field}. A name is 1 to {max} characters of lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
Ladder entry {index} declares device field {field} with a value that is empty or longer than {max} characters.
Ladder entry {index} declares {count} device fields. At most {max} ride on one entry.
Ladder entry {index} declares device field {field} on method {method}. Device fields belong to ephemeral-account; anywhere else one is a typo that would be carried silently.
policies.reject.enforcement.interactive_: enforcement.execution is no-interactive-shell, but the route still permits {request}. Deny both shell and pty-req, or choose a rung the route actually stands on.
policies.reject.enforcement.permitted_re: enforcement.execution is no-interactive-shell, but the route names no requests allow-list. A request axis nobody polices permits a shell, so the claim cannot hold.
policies.reject.enforcement.restricted_e: enforcement.execution is {rung}, but the route's filter policy is not exec_mode: restricted. That rung is the restricted allow-list applied to the account, so the two must agree.
policies.reject.enforcement.platform_rol: enforcement.execution is platform-authorized, but no platform_role is named. The role is the authorization the rung claims.
A platform_role is named, but enforcement.execution is {rung}. The role belongs to platform-authorized and means nothing elsewhere.
policies.reject.enforcement.destinations: enforcement.reach is account-egress-restricted, but no permitted_destinations are named. The destination list is what the restriction is made of.
policies.reject.enforcement.attestation_: enforcement.{axis} is platform-attested but carries no attestation. Name who asserts it (asserted_by) and the evidence (reference): this system does not verify an attested rung.
An attestation is carried, but no axis is platform-attested (execution is {execution}, reach is {reach}). An applied rung is configured by the proxy and has nobody to attribute.
policies.reject.enforcement.applied_rung: enforcement.{axis} is {rung}, which the proxy applies to an account it administers, but no ladder entry creates the account. The proxy refuses that answer outright: add an ephemeral-user or ephemeral-account entry, or use platform-attested if the target already enforces it.
policies.reject.scope.name_invalid: Scope {scope} is not a usable name. A scope name is the text a grant carries and a rule matches, so it may not be blank, padded, longer than 128 characters, or contain control characters.
policies.reject.scope.privileged_fails_o: Scope {scope} is privileged and says unanswered: open. A privileged window never counts on an unconfirmed push: use closed or outage, or leave the key out.
policies.reject.obligation.kind_missing: Obligation {index} names no kind. Use record-session, require-approval or require-step-up.
policies.reject.obligation.duplicate: Obligation {obligation} is listed twice. Remove the duplicate.
policies.reject.obligation.on_deny: A deny rule carries obligation {obligation}. Obligations are things a permitted session must do, and a denied one has none.
policies.reject.bundle.tenant_mismatch: The bundle names tenant {bundle}, but it was sent to tenant {tenant}. A bundle says which tenant it serves: change its tenant line, or send it to that tenant.
policies.reject.unknown: The compiler answered {code}, which this console has no sentence for.
policies.finding.satisfiability.proxies_: No proxy in this tenant has declared what it can serve, so no rule can be judged against a build.
policies.finding.satisfiability.no_proxy: No declaring proxy can serve the route of rule {rule}. On a proxy, a rung it cannot honour is skipped silently, so the ladder gets shorter with no error anywhere. {proxies_count, plural, one {# proxy falls} other {# proxies fall}} short.
policies.finding.satisfiability.target_c: A fresh capability record says {targets_count, plural, one {# target} other {# targets}} that rule {rule} reaches cannot take the rung it claims.
policies.finding.satisfiability.target_u: The rung rule {rule} applies is not proven on {targets_count, plural, one {# target} other {# targets}}: each one's capability record is stale, undated or absent. The absence of proof is not proof of absence.
policies.finding.authoring.interpreter_i: Rule {rule}'s restricted allow-list names {executable}, an interpreter ({interpreter}) that can hand back a shell. Under rung {rung} the list is not the boundary it claims; the real guarantee is {guarantee} at best.
policies.finding.authoring.cache_hint_ou: Rule {rule} carries a {ttl_seconds}-second cache hint, but it is gated by a condition its cache key does not carry, and no grant or duration bounds the route. A proxy would reuse the answer after the condition stops holding.
policies.finding.authoring.cache_hint_sp: Rule {rule} is gated by {term} and carries a {ttl_seconds}-second cache hint. A proxy reuses a cached decision by identity, target, port, method and hop trail, never by the client's address, so the hint admits the same identity from any address.
policies.finding.algorithm.floor_undecla: Rule {rule} sets algorithm floor {floor}, which {proxies_count, plural, one {# proxy has} other {# proxies have}} not declared, so authorize refuses the route there.
policies.finding.algorithm.axis_emptied: On {proxies_count, plural, one {# build} other {# builds}}, the bans of rule {rule} leave the {axis} axis nothing to offer under profile {profile}, so authorize refuses the route there.
policies.finding.algorithm.declaration_u: {proxies_count, plural, =0 {No build has declared the algorithms it offers, so the bans of rule {rule} cannot be judged.} one {# build's declaration cannot judge the bans of rule {rule} under profile {profile}.} other {# builds' declarations cannot judge the bans of rule {rule} under profile {profile}.}}
policies.finding.algorithm.ban_unmatched: No recorded build offers {name} on the {axis} axis. A ban of a name nothing offers changes nothing, and a typo looks exactly like a working ban.
policies.finding.algorithm.target_below_: {targets_count, plural, one {# target} other {# targets}} that rule {rule} reaches negotiated below floor {floor}. Raising the floor breaks each one.
policies.finding.algorithm.target_not_re: {targets_count, plural, one {# target} other {# targets}} that rule {rule} reaches with floor {floor} reported no key exchange, or an old one, so the floor is not shown as met there.
policies.finding.algorithm.policy_unmet: Target {unmet_target} recorded that it could not meet the {unmet_axis} algorithm policy that rule {rule} names (cause: {unmet_cause}). The record is a past observation, and the device may have changed.
policies.finding.algorithm.policy_unmet_: The read of stored unmet-policy records stopped at {limit} records, so the warnings above may miss a target.
policies.finding.unknown: {source} reported {code}, which this console has no sentence for.
error.policy_invalid: The bundle does not compile, so nothing was stored or run. Validating it shows each rejection at the line it names.
error.findings_not_accepted: This activation carries warnings that have not been accepted. Accept each by its id to publish knowingly, or change the bundle.
error.policy_blocked: A registered policy validator blocks this activation.
policies.title: Policy
policies.lede: Every stored version of this tenant's policy, newest first: the one every decision is taken under, and every one before and after it. A version is never edited. Activating any of them moves the pointer, and activating an older one is a rollback.
policies.author: Author a candidate
policies.active.title: Active now
policies.active.none: No version is active, so every decision in this tenant is the default deny until one is.
policies.table.caption: Stored policy versions, newest first
policies.table.onePage: One page of the stored versions. The list continues on the next page.
policies.partial.active: The active version's details could not be read. The list below still marks which version is active.
policies.empty.title: No policy has been uploaded
policies.empty.body: Until a version is uploaded and activated, every decision in this tenant is the default deny. Author a candidate here, validate it and upload it, or apply one from a pipeline with policyctl.
policies.version.notFound.title: That is not a version
policies.version.notFound.body: {version} is not a version number. Versions are numbered from 1 and never deleted, so a link to one must name a whole number.
policies.version.missing.title: No such version
policies.version.missing.body: This tenant stores no version {version}. Versions are numbered from 1 and never deleted, so a link to one that does not exist names another tenant's, or was mistyped.
policies.partial.report: The publish-time report could not be read, so the source is shown without its findings.
policies.source.label: Policy source
policies.rejections.title: {count, plural, one {The compiler refused the bundle: # rejection} other {The compiler refused the bundle: # rejections}}
policies.rejections.lede: Nothing was stored. Each rejection is listed here with its place, and set beneath its line in the source below.
policies.report.title: Publish-time report
policies.report.lede: Checked against the fleet as it is now. Advice stops nothing. A warning stops activation until it is accepted by its id, which the activation's record names. A blocking finding stops it outright. Activation checks again.
policies.report.counts: {blocking, plural, one {# blocking} other {# blocking}} · {warning, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}} · {advice, plural, one {# advice} other {# advice}}
policies.report.empty.title: Nothing to report
policies.report.empty.body: Every check passed against the fleet as it is now.
policies.diff.noRules: No rule was added, removed, changed or moved, and no bundle key differs.
policies.diff.moved.note: The first rule that matches answers, so a rule that moved can change which of two rules answers a question both match.
policies.diff.label: {to} against {from}
policies.sim.title: Simulate against recorded traffic
policies.sim.lede: Replays the decisions recorded in a window against this policy. It is pure: every input is the record's own, nothing is probed and nothing changes. At most 10,000 decisions are read.
policies.sim.idle: Choose a window and replay it.
policies.sim.truncated: The window holds more decisions than one replay reads. These are the first {count}.
policies.sim.empty.title: No decisions recorded in this window
policies.sim.empty.body: Replay reads only what was recorded. Choose a wider window.
policies.sim.none.title: Nothing would change
policies.sim.none.body: Every decision replayed is answered the same way.
policies.sim.col.subject: Subject
policies.sim.unreplayable.title: {count, plural, one {# decision could not be replayed} other {# decisions could not be replayed}}
policies.sim.unreplayable.lede: Each is listed, never skipped and never replayed as a different question.
policies.activate.title: Activate {version}
policies.rollback.title: Roll back to {version}
policies.activate.body: Activating {version} makes it the policy every decision in this tenant is taken under, from the next decision on. {active}, active now, stays stored and can be activated again.
policies.activate.bodyFirst: Activating {version} makes it the policy every decision in this tenant is taken under, from the next decision on.
policies.rollback.body: {version} is older than {active}, the version active now, so activating it is a rollback. Every decision from the next on is taken under {version}. {active} stays stored and can be activated again.
policies.activate.checking: Checking the publish-time report against the fleet as it is now.
policies.activate.unread: The publish-time report could not be read first. Activation checks it again, and refuses if it must.
policies.activate.hint: The name must match exactly. Decisions taken under it are not taken back by a later rollback.
policies.activate.clear: The publish-time report holds no warning and no blocking finding.
policies.activate.blocking: {count, plural, one {A blocking finding stops this activation outright.} other {# blocking findings stop this activation outright.}}
policies.activate.warnings: {total, plural, one {One warning stops this activation until it is accepted by its id.} other {# warnings stop this activation until each is accepted by its id.}} {count, plural, =0 {Each is accepted.} one {One is not accepted yet.} other {# are not accepted yet.}} The activation's record names every id accepted.
policies.activate.done: {count, plural, =0 {{version} is active.} one {{version} is active, with # warning accepted by its id.} other {{version} is active, with # warnings accepted by their ids.}}
policies.rollback.done: {count, plural, =0 {Rolled back to {version}.} one {Rolled back to {version}, with # warning accepted by its id.} other {Rolled back to {version}, with # warnings accepted by their ids.}}
policies.activate.unchanged: {version} was already active. Nothing changed and nothing was recorded.
policies.candidate.title: Candidate
policies.candidate.lede: A source not stored yet. Validate it, see what it changes and what it would have done to recorded traffic, then upload it. Nothing here changes a decision until a stored version is activated.
policies.candidate.label: Bundle (YAML)
policies.candidate.hint: Started from {version}. Your edits are kept in this tab until it closes.
policies.candidate.hintBlank: No version is active to start from. Your edits are kept in this tab until it closes.
policies.candidate.hintDraft: Your draft, kept in this tab since you last edited it.
policies.candidate.required: Write or paste a bundle first.
policies.candidate.uploaded: Uploaded as {version}. It is stored, not active.
policies.candidate.existing: This source is already stored, as {version}.
policies.candidate.stale: The source has changed since the results below were checked.
policies.candidate.idle.title: Nothing validated yet
policies.candidate.idle.body: Validate the candidate to see each rejection at its line, or the publish-time report.
policies.candidate.changes.idle.title: Not compared yet
policies.candidate.changes.idle.body: Compare the candidate with the active version to see what it adds, removes, changes and moves.
policies.candidate.unparsed.title: Nothing to compare
policies.candidate.unparsed.body: The candidate does not parse, so there is nothing to compare. Validate it to see each rejection at its line.
